Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can line up the right deployment option for FinPay:

Summary of what you shared:
- Primary use: real-time fraud-check scoring for payment flows (sub-100ms target at tail) + nightly batch model refreshes for feature engineering.
- Expected peak throughput: ~2,500 reqs/min during batch windows, ~150 reqs/sec sustained during peak business hours.
- Latency SLA: 95th percentile under 120ms; tail latency ideally <200ms.
- Data/sensitivity: PCI-adjacent; would prefer data isolation and tighter controls.

Initial recommendation (based on today's notes):
- Hosted API for quick POC and early productization if you can tolerate some multi-tenant variability during the POC.
- Dedicated capacity if you need predictable 95p latency with strict isolation and sustained throughput (we can reserve GPU pools and set latency SLOs).

Proposed next steps:
1) I can kick off a short Dedicated POC proposal that includes baseline throughput/latency targets + configuration (batching, kv-cache settings, node types).
2) Marissa (cc'd) can run a quick spike to simulate your latency profile against both Hosted and a Dedicated node config and share results.
3) If Procurement is ready, we can include a 30-day reserved capacity pilot in the quote so you get deterministic performance.

Can you confirm: 1) is isolation a hard requirement for production? 2) do you have a preferred go/no-go metric for the POC (e.g., 95p latency <120ms)?

I attached the draft FinPay-Latency-Profile.xlsx you shared and a short proposal outline.

Thanks — copying a few technical notes so Samir and Procurement have the right expectations.

Internal TL;DR for your POC: Dedicated capacity is the safer bet given the 95p <120ms requirement and sustained 150 rps. Here's why:
- Deterministic resource allocation: reserved GPU pools avoid noisy-neighbor variance that can affect tail latency.
- Batching & KV-cache tuning: on Dedicated we can aggressively tune continuous batching and KV caching for your seq-length distribution; on Hosted we can do these too but less control.
- Autoscaling behavior: Hosted can scale quickly but may introduce brief cold-starts for certain model variants — can be mitigated by warm pools, but differs by plan.

Suggested Dedicated POC configuration:
- Node type: 4x A100-equivalent with 200GB aggregated memory (config depends on model size)
- Network: colocated region (us-west) + private peering to keep RTT low
- SLOs for pilot: 95p latency target <120ms, 99p <300ms, sustain 150 rps for 2 hours in load window

Test plan:
- Redwood will run synthetic traffic (we'll share cfg) + you run representative requests from your staging infra.
- We'll capture token-level latencies and a per-route breakdown in the Console.

I'll prepare a short POC scope doc and a preliminary quote. Neha — I suggest we attach the quote and a proposed SOW to Procurement so they can start approvals.
